steps.label: (A - lambda I)v = 0 needs a singular matrix
steps.sub: A nonzero v only exists if det(A - lambda I) = 0

steps.label: det(A - lambda I) = 0 is a polynomial in lambda

code:
Z = [[1,0],[0,-1]]

det(Z - lambda*I) = (1-lambda)(-1-lambda) = lambda^2 - 1

lambda^2 - 1 = 0  ->  lambda = 1 or lambda = -1
caption: Pauli-Z has exactly two eigenvalues: +1 and -1.
Both eigenvector/eigenvalue pairs confirmed by plugging straight back into Av = lambda v.

eyebrow: The Headline of the Whole Chapter

steps.label: (1,0) is exactly |0>, (0,1) is exactly |1>
steps.sub: Not a coincidence engineered for the example

steps.label: This is why Z represents a computational-basis measurement
steps.sub: Lesson 19 builds the whole measurement story on this exact fact
